subject.title: fix(matrix): tolerate SAS accept events missing method

question: Should OpenClaw accept this private matrix-js-sdk `cryptoBackend.preprocessToDeviceMessages` wrapper for the Matrix SAS missing-method compatibility bug after live proof is supplied?
rationale: The code path is the narrow place that sees the malformed to-device event before Rust crypto rejects it, but it is a private dependency boundary inside E2EE verification and needs maintainer ownership beyond normal green CI.

options.title: Require proof, then accept the wrapper
options.body: Have the contributor or a maintainer add redacted live Element/Synapse verification proof from this branch, then merge if maintainers accept the private hook.

options.title: Pause for upstream or public seam
options.body: Hold the PR and pursue an upstream matrix-js-sdk or Matrix SDK public compatibility point instead of wrapping `cryptoBackend`.

options.title: Accept the private hook without more proof
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly override the proof gate, but they would own the live-behavior and future-upgrade uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept the wrapper
recommendation.body: Have the contributor or a maintainer add redacted live Element/Synapse verification proof from this branch, then merge if maintainers accept the private hook.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history around Matrix E2EE identity trust and verification internals adjacent to this boundary.
